highlights: A weak day on 13 Nov: banks fell (HNB −1.88%, Sampath −1.91%, NDB and NTB −1.29%, DFCC −2.80%) with Commercial Bank flat, and John Keells slipped 1.52%; Dialog (+0.40%) and Ceylon Tobacco (+1.05%) held up.

Dipped Products' September quarter: revenue Rs 25.3bn (+19.5% year on year) and EPS Rs 2.53 (+64.4%), its best quarter in two years; P/E 9.5x and P/B 1.15x at Rs 71.10. The shares rose 3.94% on 13 Nov.
Ceylon Tobacco declared a third interim dividend of Rs 41.00 (XD 23 Nov, paid 11 Dec); the broker puts the trailing dividend yield at 8.9% at Rs 1,809.50.
2027 Budget: tax relief for the middle class and record capital spending; the President said public debt should fall to 87% of GDP by 2032, better than the earlier 95% target.
No new broker ratings or targets, so nothing to set against the site's fair values.

news.title: Dipped Products: Q2 2026/27 results
news.text: Revenue Rs 25,338mn against Rs 21,196mn a year earlier (+19.5%), up 1.25% on the June quarter. EPS Rs 2.53 against Rs 1.54 (+64.4%), up from Rs 2.06 in the June quarter. The broker's card shows a trailing P/E of 9.53x and P/B of 1.15x at the 12 Nov close of Rs 71.10.

news.title: 2027 Budget
news.text: The President, also finance minister, presented the government's third budget: middle-class tax relief, record capital spending, and a forecast that public debt falls to 87% of GDP by 2032 (earlier target 95%).

news.title: Private credit
news.text: Private-sector credit reached Rs 2.1tn in the first nine months of 2026, with short-term loans taking a larger share; lawmakers asked whether enough is going into new investment and capacity.

news.title: Trade and exports
news.text: Sri Lanka is seeking a new free trade agreement with China, and officials reviewed progress towards the US$5bn ICT/BPM export target for 2030.

news.title: Hayleys Solar
news.text: Hayleys Solar opened what it calls Sri Lanka's first 24/7 renewable energy operations centre, monitoring renewable assets from one digital platform.

news.title: Global
news.text: India is buying more Gulf crude as Russian oil loses its price advantage; US shares closed lower as Nvidia fell after news of its CEO's exit outweighed gains in energy stocks.
